### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**19** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6c96b37be84c496bf3e0dd4b89cd17999a0f4f62` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d79a374a1b3dd100f13f77a912c06fcf4082b410` — the merge of head `252a378f9908e75d931168a222b3c868e74ea2e4` into base `6c96b37be84c496bf3e0dd4b89cd17999a0f4f62`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d79a374a1b3dd100f13f77a912c06fcf4082b410 && git checkout d79a374a1b3dd100f13f77a912c06fcf4082b410
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6c96b37be84c496bf3e0dd4b89cd17999a0f4f62 252a378f9908e75d931168a222b3c868e74ea2e4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6c96b37be84c496bf3e0dd4b89cd17999a0f4f62 && git merge --no-ff 252a378f9908e75d931168a222b3c868e74ea2e4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6c96b37be84c496bf3e0dd4b89cd17999a0f4f62
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `252a378f9908e75d931168a222b3c868e74ea2e4`
Local-runs: none

Read-only, at tier, adversarial to the dispatch. Inputs: card #20513 (body and all 25 comments — the census 5900801368, the ruling 5902360492 「20513 A」 A / A, the stage-4 claim 5912562820, the stage-4 `os-dev-report` 5913433803), PR #20877 (body, 8-file list, the net diff `origin/main...252a378f99` at merge base `72f8c3820`), PR #20795 at `df67985b0` with its record 5906164285 (which held the three `driver-sql` aggregate refusals for their twins) and PR #20848 at `a94f3bad3` with its record 5910833957 as the prior applications of the same ruling, the head's check-runs, the 16 cited objectstack cards, and the head's own source through `git show` / `git grep` / `git diff`. Nothing built, run or re-run; no worktree, no checkout. The PR head was confirmed as `252a378f9908e75d931168a222b3c868e74ea2e4` (branch `claude/issue-20513-stage4-driver-turso`, draft, `Part of #20513`, no closing keyword) before the read and had not moved.

**Check-runs on `252a378f99`, read once for this record at 2026-09-30T14:45Z and not polled:** 32 check-runs — 24 `completed` / `success` (Build Core, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Part-of PR must not also close its card, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, the two claim / single-writer guards, Dogfood Regression Gate and its three shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Test Core 1/6, 2/6 and 4/6, Type Check · source gates, · debt ledger and · consumer gates, Auto Label, filter), 3 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke — path-filtered), 5 `in_progress` (Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core 3/6, 5/6 and 6/6, Type Check · workspace), 0 `failure`. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts: the runs still going carry `check:doc-authoring` (Lint & Repo Gates) and part of the driver suites (Test Core). Temporal Conformance, which runs the whole `driver-sql` suite against live PG and MySQL, is `success`. This record judges the contract on the diff, the cards and the head's source; a `failure` among the five open runs, if one lands, is a new fact for the adopting session, not one this record has read.

### ① Derived judgments

**Scope against the ruling and the claim — right.** The ruling orders stages per package until the ledger is empty, all three categories, form D, `--census-ledger` in the same PR, author-visible text first and log lines last; the claim scopes stage 4 to `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/**`, the three held `driver-sql` aggregate rows, the pins, the ledger and one `patch` changeset for both packages, and forbids wire `code` / field / status changes, comment or docblock edits (#20595) and any other package's ledger rows. The 8-file list is exactly that surface: 4 source files (3 in `driver-turso`, `sql-driver.ts`), 2 test files, the ledger, the changeset. No governed path. The order inside the stage is honoured as commit order (`fe71ac88e` the aggregate family on both faces, `ab16ca922` the filter refusals and the `auto_number` refusal, `8c754165` the three log lines, `252a378f9` the changeset); 32 literals sit under the stop line, so nothing was left to split.

**Text only — right, checked line by line.** Every removed and added line in the four source files carries a string-literal delimiter; a filter of the diff for changed lines without one returns nothing. No `err.code`, `err.status`, `StandardErrorCode` member, exported symbol, field name, branch or call moves: every `throw`, `return this.withheldRefusal(`, `logger?.info?.(` / `logger?.warn(` call and its second argument is a context line. `auto_number` still maps to `TEXT` (remote-transport.ts about 2695). Comments and docblocks are untouched — the diff contains no comment line, and the bare cloud ids in `remote-transport.ts`'s docblocks are still there on the head (③). The dev's scanner-skeleton claim is consistent with this reading; what this record verified is the diff itself.

**Accept-set and public surface — nothing moves — right.** No schema, filter grammar, DDL, route, wire `code`, HTTP status, field name, default or export changes; a caller sees different prose in the same envelopes (`INVALID_QUERY` / 400, `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` / 501, `INVALID_FILTER` / 400). No added line carries a tracker id (0 hits over the diff's `+` lines).

**Ledger diff — right, exact, recounted.** Parsing the baseline at `origin/main` and at the head: files 204 to 200, (file, id) pairs 514 to 485, occurrences 769 to 722. Exactly four rows leave and no row is added or changed: `remote-transport.ts` 22 pairs / 40 occurrences, `turso-driver.ts` 2 / 2, `remote-canonical-backfill.ts` 2 / 2, `sql-driver.ts` 3 / 3 (`#5907`, `#10413`, `#6409` — the three stage 1 held). Reconciled against the source diff: the removed lines carrying an id are 25 in `remote-transport.ts` (40 id occurrences), 2 (2) in `turso-driver.ts`, 2 (2) in the backfill, 3 (3) in `sql-driver.ts` — 47, matching the PR body's 32 literals / 47 occurrences once the five two-literal `+` chains are counted as the dev counts them. A `git grep` of the head over the four files finds no tracker id on any non-comment line holding a string delimiter. `check:doc-authoring` inside Lint & Repo Gates is the mechanical confirmation, pending at read time.

**The three held pairs — right, both faces in one commit, and they read identically.** At the head the function bodies of `undeclaredAggregateFunctionError` and `refuseDistinctAggregateWithoutField` are byte-identical between `sql-driver.ts` and `remote-transport.ts` (a `diff` of the two extracted bodies is empty for each). The per-aggregation `filter` pair differs only by the backend-name interpolation (`${backend}` against the literal `Turso remote transport`) and `return` against `throw` — both pre-existing, the message text otherwise identical. The two pairs stage 1 left differing by the citation only now differ by nothing in their text: the declared-but-uncompiled pair by the list constant's name only (`SQL_AGGREGATE_FUNCTIONS` / `REMOTE_AGGREGATE_FUNCTIONS`, which the parity test says render the same six functions today), the date-bucket pair by the `Bucketed here:` interpolation that each face fills for itself, whose pinned contract is first-sentence parity (`remote-transport-groupby-node.test.ts` about 460-463, "the tails differ on purpose"). The pins compare runtime messages from the two packages, not two copies of a literal: `remote-transport-aggregate-function-refusal.test.ts` about 348 (`expect(remote.message).toBe(local.message)` over `median` / `array_agg` / `string_agg`) and `remote-transport-undeclared-aggregate-keys.test.ts` about 201. The dev's ablation (10 of 33 red with the `driver-sql` face alone re-cited) is its own measurement; the byte identity on the head is what this record verified. `sql-driver.ts`'s row leaves the ledger, so stage 1's hold is discharged.

**Form D, string by string — right.** All 15 cited objectstack issues read `closed` / `completed` and PR #5368 is merged; no cited decision has been reversed. The 10 cloud-repository ids (1003, 1004, 1005, 1051, 1058, 1066, 1073, 1075, 1076, 1116) are not readable from this repository and resolve here to unrelated cards, as the dev says; those sentences were judged against the head's code and the file's own docblocks. The four literals that gained words, each judged against the card and the head's code:
- Non-boolean `$null` diagnostic (5347, 5368, cloud 1116): "Every driver now refuses it, so one filter no longer gets a different answer per backend." True on the head for all five drivers: `driver-sql` throws `nonBooleanNullComparandError` on an own, non-boolean `$null` (`sql-driver.ts` about 4972-4977), inherited by `driver-sqlite-wasm` (`extends SqlDriver`) and by Turso local; `driver-memory`'s single door `assertFilterConditionShape` refuses it (`filter-refusal.ts` about 937) and is called on the matcher (`memory-matcher.ts` about 55), the query path (`memory-driver.ts` about 1361) and the analytics face (`memory-analytics.ts` about 1592); `driver-mongodb` throws on its walk (`mongodb-filter.ts` about 303-306); the remote transport in this very method. The historical clauses the sentence keeps ("compiled IS NULL … compiled IS NOT NULL … dropped the constraint entirely") are past tense and are what #5347 measured. "Driver" rather than "evaluator" is exact: `@objectstack/formula`'s `matchesFilter` answers a non-`true` `$null` as not-null (`matches-filter.ts` about 719) — ③ item for reach. No pin compares this diagnostic byte for byte with the local face (`turso-local-remote-null-parity.test.ts` uses `toContain` on the shared requirement sentence; the seam test's parity is over the short withheld sentence, which is unchanged), so words added on the remote face alone break nothing. #5347's title is the opposite-answers finding, #5368 the landing that refuses at the door.
- Remote `auto_number` refusal (6944): "It is refused rather than resolved, because resolving would write NULL into the slot and persist the row without its record number." `refuseRemoteAutonumber` is thrown by `refuseUngeneratableRemoteAutonumber` on `create` (`turso-driver.ts` about 2376), on `bulkCreate` (about 3048) and on an `upsert` that cannot merge (about 2431); `RemoteTransport.create` builds its own `INSERT INTO … VALUES` (`remote-transport.ts` about 1768) and the transport never references `fillAutoNumberFields`; the slot is a `TEXT` column. That the un-refused leg persists the row with a NULL number is exactly what #7099 records, and the unnumbered-upsert warning three lines down (about 2358: "the row is persisted, its record number is not") says the same for the leg the refusal cannot classify. #6944's title is this gap ("remote 面根本不生成自增号 … 自建 INSERT"). The replaced clause ("Until this change the same call RESOLVED and wrote NULL") described history; the new one is present tense and true.
- Backfill info line (5770): "the converted rows now hold the one canonical text form, and the column drops the unindexable read-side repair only once a pass finds nothing left to convert." The converge and epoch `UPDATE`s set the column to the canonical expression; the mark is `base.canonical = after.residual === 0 && after.epochInBand === 0` on a post-pass probe, under the comment "The ONLY thing that earns the mark: nothing is left for either phase to change", and the module header says "Marked only when proved". The info line prints with `canonical: report.canonical` in its payload, so a pass that converted rows without earning the mark says so. #5770 is the remote backfill channel ("分批、可恢复、完成标记"). True.
- Unresolvable-remainder warning (cloud 1005): "a value that cannot be read as an instant is counted and reported, never guessed at." `unresolvedEpochTextRows = max(0, after.epochText − after.epochInBand)`; the epoch phase's `WHERE` selects the in-band rows only, so out-of-band digit rows are not written; the count reaches the operator through this warn and the report. The module docblock (about 81) records the same rule in the file's own words ("rather than guessed at"). True.

Where only the citation goes (28 literals): each sentence already carried the decision and is otherwise unchanged, and each readable card's title matches its sentence — the undeclared-function (5907), declared-but-uncompiled (5907), field-less `count_distinct` (6409), per-aggregation `filter` (10413) and date-bucket (6212) refusals on the remote face and the three `driver-sql` twins; the non-boolean `$exists` diagnostic (5347, 5369, 5903); the unlowered `$between` (cloud 1003), unsupported operator (cloud 1004), undeclared combinator both arms (5769, 5348), non-list combinator (5769), undefined comparand (6050 — the "Undefined binding(s)" / IS NULL split is its title), non-node operand both arms (cloud 1051, 1076 / 1004, 1058, 1066, 1073), non-object `where` (cloud 1004, 1058, 1066, 1073, 1075), empty operator map (cloud 1004, 1058, 1066), the withheld cross-field sentence (cloud 1058, 7929) and the unbindable-comparand diagnostic and wire sentence (cloud 1004, 1058, 8197); the unnumbered-upsert warning (7099). The withheld-detail sentences ("withheld from the message; the full diagnostic is in the server log") now read as `driver-sql`'s do after stage 1.

**Pins — right, 2 tests in 2 files.** `remote-transport-null-comparand-refusal.test.ts` about 177-183 now asserts "It is refused rather than coerced" and the full "Every driver now refuses it, so one filter no longer gets a different answer per backend." — both present in the head's runtime string (the second spans a `+` boundary in the source and is one sentence at runtime); the title moved with the assertions, which is right, since the old title described asserting ids. `remote-transport-comparand-refusal.test.ts` 234 asserts `indistinguishable from "no rows matched".` on the unbindable-comparand refusal, whose line 233 already ties it to the comparand-type sentence; the phrase is on the head at about 4714 (and, with the same period, in the unsupported-operator sentence — harmless, since the test's own `find` produces the comparand refusal). The dev's mutation legs (1 / 54, 1 / 26) are its own measurement. No test outside `driver-turso` pins a changed string; the one lookalike is `rest`'s fixture (③).

**Review faces — right, with one wording note.** The changeset (below) reads as a CHANGELOG entry: every family it names is in the diff, and each sentence it summarises matches the string. The PR body's table, counts, commit order and ledger numbers match the diff and the recount above; it carries `Clause-②: no` at line start and no closing keyword. The note: the changeset says the declared-but-uncompiled and date-bucket refusals "read exactly like the SQL driver's again" — exact for the sentence templates, while the rendered date-bucket line still names each face's own bucketed list (the declared asymmetry its pin protects). Not a false statement of behaviour; carrier: whoever next edits that changeset, if anyone does before release.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/20513-driver-turso-runtime-strings-state-the-decision.md`: `'@objectstack/driver-turso': patch` and `'@objectstack/driver-sql': patch` — right. Both packages are released (`17.5.0`, not private); the diff publishes changed prose in those two packages and nothing else — no key, export, envelope `code`, status or default moves — so this is a fix-class patch in each, never `skip-changeset`. The body is CHANGELOG-fit: it names the message families, says which sentences gained words and what they now say, and closes "Text only: no error code, field name, status or behaviour changes". No model identifier in the changeset, the four commit trailers (`Claude-Session` plus a model-free `Co-authored-by`) or the PR body (session-URL footer) — the shape stages 1 to 3 landed with. Check Changeset is `success`.

Clause-②: no — right. Nothing an author can write is widened or narrowed; the PR body carries `Clause-②: no` at line start and the changeset repeats it.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (report 5913433803), each answered:
1. **Base `72f8c3820`, `main` not merged before the PR — accepted.** The merge base of `origin/main` and the head is `72f8c3820154c69cdf9faa6f887dc544e4c4b823`; at read time `origin/main` (`07356a6ab0`) is 7 commits past it, and `git log` over the 8 changed paths between the two is empty — none touches these files or the ledger. CI tests the merge ref, and every completed run is green.
2. **Two pins re-pinned, one title changed with its assertions — verified in ①.**
3. **Cloud ids in `remote-transport.ts` comments and docblocks (carrier #20595) — accepted.** Comments are outside the ruling and untouched in the diff; the head's docblocks still carry them, which is #20595's surface.
4. **`driver-memory`'s `nonBooleanNullComparandError` still cites `#5347` (carrier: stage 5) — accepted, and verified.** `filter-refusal.ts` about 617 ends "(#5347)."; its ledger row is another package's, which the claim forbids; the leading sentence is the verbatim twin and the two faces now differ by the citation only, exactly the situation stage 1 left the remote aggregate pairs in. Held, not lost.
5. **`rest`'s truncation fixture (carrier: none) — accepted as stated.** `rest-4xx-message-truncation.test.ts` 52-59 builds its own copy of `driver-sql`'s `$null` sentence with "(#5347)."; a `.test.ts` file outside the ledger, and its assertions (about 104-105) check the operator / field / spec sentence, never the citation, and never compare with a driver's text.
6. **Test titles carrying cloud ids (carrier: none) — accepted.** 31 `describe` / `it` titles in `driver-turso`'s test files carry a four-digit cloud id; test files are outside the ledger and outside the ruling's shipped-`src/` scope.
7. **The seam test's now-identity strip (carrier: none) — accepted.** `remote-transport-compile-refusal-seam.test.ts` about 619 still derives the remote `$between` arity sentence as `[RemoteTransport]` plus the local one with `/ \(#\d+\)/g` stripped; neither face carries a parenthesised id now, so the strip is an identity. What it would tolerate — a citation returning on the local face alone — is what `check:doc-authoring`'s growth refusal exists for, so the tolerance is harmless. Carrier none is right.
8. **`@objectstack/formula` `matchesFilter` answering a non-`true` `$null` as not-null — a reading only, not a defect worth a card, and here is the reach that says so.** The arm is `case '$null': return v === true ? actual == null : actual != null` (`matches-filter.ts` about 719), the same two-branch shape #5347 measured on the drivers. Its callers on the head hand it filters no author writes raw: the RLS write-side `check` (`security-plugin.ts` about 3226, step 3.6) and the delegator check come from `computeWriteCheckFilter`, and a policy's `check` is a CEL string by schema (`rls.zod.ts` about 499) that `compileCelToFilter` lowers to `$null: true` / `$null: false` only (`cel-to-filter.ts` about 668 and 673); the tenant wall (about 3530) is computed by the plugin; the explain engine (about 964) reads the same compiled policies; `objectql`'s HAVING (`having-filter.ts` about 1208) hands it a single resolved operator after its own admission walk. No public door hands the evaluator a non-boolean `$null`, and the evaluator's own header declares a total, answer-not-throw posture with three ruled exceptions (#5240, #19886, #20355). Making `$null` a fourth would be a ruling of the #5240 kind, not a bug fix; the sentence's "every driver" is the exact claim. Carrier none, as the dev says — recorded here so a later reader has the measurement.
9. **Commit trailers (the model-free pair, not the harness reminder's line) — accepted,** as stages 1 to 3 were under AGENTS.md's rule.
10. **NOT MEASURED locally (live PG / MySQL, Test Core shards, Dogfood, workspace type-check) — CI's;** at read time Temporal Conformance, Dogfood and its three shards, Build Core, Test Core 1/6, 2/6 and 4/6 and three of the four type-check lanes are `success`, the rest `in_progress`, none `failure`.

`open_questions`: none in the stage-4 report; none raised here. The census reconciles as the dev states: its `driver-turso` row is 24 messages with "id occurrences 44", and the ledger at the base held 44 across 3 files; the 20 line-site entries in the census's per-file list fold the `+` chains the same way. The card stays open for stage 5 (`driver-memory` and the other packages, plus the `engine.ts` `#4419` row stage 3 held); the lane children (#20749, #20751, #20753, `Blocked-by: #20513`) are unaffected; the ledger's other rows are untouched.
